author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: WithSecure Elements has no webhook, and the Elements Connector's syslog layout isn't published, so these parsers read security events and audit logs pulled from the Elements API by the example bridge in bridges/withsecure-elements-events and posted to HTTP Ingest. The bridge names each record in withsecure_record. With partner-level API credentials one bridge reads every company under the partner, and organization_name in the metadata says which. Malware found by file, manual and real-time scanning, AMSI and DeepGuard goes to Antivirus. Every other security event (EDR incidents and their updates, firewall, web and connection blocks, application and device control, tamper protection, Collaboration Protection, settings) goes to Thirdparty, with an EDR incident's risk as the severity and otherwise critical as HIGH, warning as MEDIUM and info as INFO. Administrator logins in the audit log go to Auth, with the address and browser read from the description, and other audit log actions go to CloudAudit. Each event's details object is kept as JSON. The event reference names the infection infectionName and the file path, while some API events carry name and filePath, and engine names differ in case and wording between the reference and the API (amsi and AMSI); the parsers read both. Samples follow the API envelope and the per-type details in WithSecure's Security Events reference, with made-up values. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-15 (237 of 237 fields matched the emulator, in 3 runs), and each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent. No built-in parser in that tenant claimed these events in 3 Run Tests.
